4900.full: 1. a vase-shaped basket , Lat. calathus, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a cooling-vessel, cooler , Virgil (ML)

4901.full: κίνησις, -εως, ἡ (κινέω), [in LXX: Job.16:6 (5), (נִיד), al. ;] a moving: Jhn.5:3.† (AS)

s: any vessel, a vase, jar, urn
4903.full: 1. the hollow of a shield or breastplate, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. any vessel, a vase, jar, urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πλεκτὸν κ. a basket, (Euripides) 3. anything that contains the body , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: to obtain by lot, to obtain

4904.full: λαγχάνω [in LXX: 1Ki.14:47 (לָכַד, see Th., Gr., 38), Wis.8:19, 3Mac 61 * ;] __1. to obtain by lot, to obtain (in cl., with genitive): with inf. art. (B1., § 36, 3; 71, 3), Luk.1:9; with accusative of thing(s), Act.1:17, 2Pe.1:1. __2. to draw lots: before περί, Jhn.19:24 (AS)

4909.full: λιθό-στρωτος, -ον (στρώννυμι), [in LXX: 2Ch.7:3, Est.1:6, Sng.3:10 (רִצְפָּה, רָצַף)* ;] paved with stones, esp. of tessallated work (Ca, i.e.); as subst., τὸ λ., a tessallated pavement: Jhn.19:13 (cf. Γαββαθᾶ).† (AS)

4910.full: λιπαρός, -ά, -όν (λίπος, fat), [in LXX: Jdg.3:29, Neh.9:35, Is 30:23 (שָׁמֵן)* ;] oily, fatty; metaphorically, of living, rich, dainty: τὰ λ. καὶ τ. λαμπρά, Rev.18:14.† (AS)

4911.full: λουτρόν, -οῦ, τό (λούω), [in LXX: Sng.4:2 6:5, (6) (רַחְצָה), Sir.34:25 * ;] a washing, bath: τ. ὕδατος, Eph.5:26; τ. παλιγγενεσίας, Tit.3:5 (see AR, Eph., l.with).† (AS)

4912.full: 1. the mane on the neck and back of certain animals, the mane of horses, the bristly back of boars and hyaenas, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the back-fin of fishes, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

Of persons and their mode of living; __(a) mild, gentle; __(b) soft, effeminate: 1Co.6:9 (prob. in obscene sense, cf. Deiss., LAE, 150, 4; MM, xvi; Zorell, see word).† (AS)

4921.full: 1. an oracle , i. e., 2. an oracular response , (Odyssey by Homer), attic 3. the seat of an oracle , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

4923.full: 1. high-minded, noble, generous , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. in bad sense, arrogant : adverb -όνως, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

4932.full: μετ-αίρω [in LXX: 4Ki.16:17 25:11, Psa.80:8, Pro.22:28 (סוּר hi., גָּלָה hi., etc.)* ;] __1. trans., to remove (LXX, ll. with). __2. (not cl.) to depart: Mat.13:53 19:1 (cf. Aq.: Gen.12:9).† (AS)

4942.full: 1. = μύρτος, (Pindar) 2. a branch or wreath of myrtle , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

4947.full: 1. a feeding-place for cattle, pasture , (Homer); ν. ὕλης a woodland pasture , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. herbage , (Homeric Hymns):—;generally, food , (Hesiod) 3. metaphorically, ἐπέων πολὺς νομός a wide range for words, (Iliad by Homer) 4. an abode allotted or assigned to one, a district, province , (Pindar), etc.; νομὸν ἔχειν to have one's dwelling-place , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. one of the districts into which Egypt was divided, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; applied also to other provinces , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

4963.full: 1. the site of a house , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. the house itself, a building , (Thucydides) (ML)

4983.full: παρά-δοσις, -εως, ἡ (παραδίδωμι), [in LXX: Est.7:26 (אֵסוּר), Jer.32:4 (נָתַן ni.), Jer.34:2 * ;] __1. a handing down or over, transfer, transmission (Arist., Polyb., al., LXX). __2. tradition of doctrine (Plat., Epict., al.); by meton., of the doctrine itself : Mat.15:2-3, 6, Mrk.7:3, 1Co.11:2, Gal.1:14, Col.2:8, 2Th.2:15 3:9.† (AS)

4990.full: 1. to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to shackle, trammel, constrain , (Homer); with infinitive to constrain one to do a thing, (Homer) (ML)

s: to be brought to an end, be finished
to repeat from beginning to end

4999.full: 1. with two right hands , i.e. using both hands alike , (Iliad by Homer) 2. very dexterous , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)
